title: CPC & Limitation
sub: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 & Limitation Act, 1963 · Osmania LLB (3 YDC) Sem V
journey: A civil case travels from the court’s door (jurisdiction) through pleadings, trial, decree and execution, may branch to special suits and appeals — and the clock of limitation runs beside it all.

stations.name: CPC basics
stations.one: Procedure is the road map to enforce civil rights: 158 sections (power) + 51 Orders (method).
stations.boss: Sangram Singh v Election Tribunal (1955) — procedure is the handmaid of justice
stations.hook: Sections = power · Orders = method

stations.name: Suit of civil nature
stations.one: A civil court tries every civil suit unless a law expressly or impliedly bars it.
stations.boss: Dhulabhai v State of MP (1968) — exclusion is never lightly inferred
stations.hook: C-B: Civil + not Barred

stations.name: Place of suing
stations.one: Lowest competent court; land → where it lies; wrongs → where done or defendant lives; rest → defendant’s home or cause of action.
stations.boss: ABC Laminart v A.P. Agencies (1989) — choose between competent courts only
stations.hook: Land → land · Wrong → spot or home · Rest → home or cause

stations.name: Res sub judice
stations.one: A later suit on the same matter between the same parties is stayed while the earlier one is pending.
stations.boss: Indian Bank v Maharashtra State Co-op Marketing Fed. (1998) — only the trial is stayed
stations.hook: Pending → pause

stations.name: Res judicata
stations.one: A matter heard and finally decided between the same parties by a competent court can’t be reopened.
stations.boss: Satyadhyan Ghosal v Deorajin Debi (1960) — RJ binds even later stages of the same case
stations.hook: D-S-T-C-F: Directly · Same parties · Title · Competent · Finally decided

stations.name: Parties to a suit
stations.one: Join all who must be there; a necessary party’s absence is fatal, a proper party’s is not.
stations.boss: Kasturi v Iyyamperumal (2005) — necessary = no effective decree without him
stations.hook: Necessary = can’t decide without him

stations.name: Cause of action & frame
stations.one: Sue for the whole claim in one suit; a part left out can’t be sued for later.
stations.boss: Gurbux Singh v Bhooralal (1964) — the bar needs the same cause of action
stations.hook: Sue for all or lose the rest

stations.name: Summons
stations.one: The court calls the defendant: personal → family → affixing → substituted service (also e-mail, courier).
stations.hook: P-F-A-S: Personal · Family · Affix · Substituted

stations.name: Pleadings
stations.one: Each side’s written case: material facts only — not law, not evidence — concisely.
stations.boss: Ram Sarup Gupta v Bishun Narain (1987) — read pleadings as a whole, not hyper-technically
stations.hook: F-M-N-C: Facts · Material · Not evidence · Concise

stations.name: Amendment
stations.one: Allowed at any stage to decide the real controversy; after trial starts only if earlier impossible despite due diligence.
stations.boss: Revajeetu Builders v Narayanaswamy (2009) — tests for allowing amendment
stations.hook: Real question yes · new case no

stations.name: Plaint
stations.one: The plaintiff’s pleading: court, parties, facts, cause of action, jurisdiction, valuation, relief.
stations.boss: T. Arivandandam v T.V. Satyapal (1977) — nip vexatious suits in the bud
stations.hook: Who · What · When · Where · Why · Want

stations.name: Return v rejection
stations.one: Wrong court → plaint returned; no cause of action / undervalued / barred → plaint rejected.
stations.boss: Saleem Bhai v State of Maharashtra (2003) — r.11 judged on the plaint alone
stations.hook: Wrong door → return · dead case → reject

stations.name: Written statement
stations.one: Defendant’s reply in 30 days (outer limit 90; commercial 120 strict); deny specifically or it’s admitted.
stations.boss: Kailash v Nanhku (2005) — the 90-day limit is directory
stations.hook: 30 → 90 (120 strict for commercial)

stations.name: Set-off & counter-claim
stations.one: Set-off: an ascertained sum the plaintiff owes; counter-claim: any claim, treated as a cross-suit.
stations.boss: Ashok Kumar Kalra v Surendra Agnihotri (2019) — counter-claim before issues, ordinarily
stations.hook: Set-off = shield · Counter-claim = sword

stations.name: Issues & S.89
stations.one: The questions the court must answer — framed at the first hearing; ADR referral where settlement is possible.
stations.boss: Afcons Infrastructure v Cherian Varkey (2010) — how to apply S.89
stations.hook: Issues = the exam paper of the suit

stations.name: Documents
stations.one: Discovery, production, admission and marking of documents; impounding and return.
stations.hook: Produce · Admit · Mark · Return

stations.name: Appearance & default
stations.one: Plaintiff absent → suit dismissed; defendant absent though served → ex parte hearing.
stations.boss: Sangram Singh v Election Tribunal (1955) — ex parte doesn’t shut the defendant out
stations.hook: Absent plaintiff loses · absent defendant goes ex parte

stations.name: Setting aside ex parte
stations.one: Decree set aside if summons not duly served or sufficient cause shown — apply in 30 days; or appeal.
stations.boss: Bhanu Kumar Jain v Archana Kumar (2005) — both remedies co-exist
stations.hook: Not served or good cause → set aside

stations.name: Witnesses
stations.one: List witnesses, summon them, pay expenses; President, Governors etc. exempt from appearing.
stations.hook: List · Summon · Pay · Examine

stations.name: Examination & affidavits
stations.one: Evidence in chief may be by affidavit; cross-examination in court or before a commissioner.
stations.boss: Salem Advocate Bar Assn v Union of India (2005) — the 1999/2002 amendments upheld
stations.hook: Chief by affidavit · cross in court

stations.name: Admissions
stations.one: Admitted facts need no proof; the court may pass judgment on admissions at any stage.
stations.boss: Uttam Singh Duggal v United Bank (2000) — judgment on clear admissions
stations.hook: Admitted = proved

stations.name: Adjournments & costs
stations.one: No more than three adjournments to a party; costs follow the event; costs for false claims and delay.
stations.hook: 3 adjournments max · costs follow the event

stations.name: Judgment, decree, order
stations.one: Judgment = reasons; decree = formal adjudication (preliminary / final); order = any other decision.
stations.hook: Reasons → judgment · Rights → decree · Rest → order

stations.name: Temporary injunction
stations.one: Preserve the property till trial: prima facie case + balance of convenience + irreparable injury.
stations.boss: Dalpat Kumar v Prahlad Singh (1992) — the three-fold test
stations.hook: P-B-I

stations.name: Receiver & commission
stations.one: Court-appointed receiver manages disputed property; commissioners examine witnesses, inspect, account.
stations.hook: Receiver = court’s caretaker

stations.name: Before-judgment orders & caveat
stations.one: Arrest or attachment before judgment to stop a defendant defeating the decree; caveat gives notice of applications.
stations.hook: Run away? arrest · Sell off? attach · Fear ex parte? caveat

stations.name: Execution — who & how
stations.one: The court that passed the decree (or the one it transfers to) executes it; questions between parties decided by it.
stations.hook: Decree is paper; execution is power

stations.name: Modes of execution
stations.one: Delivery of property, attachment and sale, arrest and detention, receiver, or any other mode the decree needs.
stations.boss: Jolly George Varghese v Bank of Cochin (1980) — no arrest without ability to pay
stations.hook: D-A-A-R-O: Deliver · Attach · Arrest · Receiver · Other

stations.name: Attachment & sale
stations.one: Debtor’s property attached and sold; tools, clothes, pension, part of salary etc. are exempt.
stations.hook: Some things the law never lets you take

stations.name: Restitution & inherent power
stations.one: Undo what was done under a decree later reversed; the court’s inherent power fills gaps.
stations.hook: Actus curiae neminem gravabit

stations.name: Suits against Government
stations.one: Two months’ notice first; urgent relief with leave; decree executable only after three months.
stations.boss: Ghanshyam Dass v Dominion of India (1984) — no fresh notice by legal heirs
stations.hook: 2-2-3: notice 2 m · leave if urgent · execute after 3 m

stations.name: Public matters
stations.one: Public nuisance and public trusts: suit by the Advocate General or two persons with leave.
stations.hook: AG or 2 with leave

stations.name: Minors & unsound mind
stations.one: A minor sues by a next friend and is defended by a guardian ad litem; compromise needs leave.
stations.hook: Next friend to sue · guardian to defend

stations.name: Indigent persons
stations.one: A person too poor to pay court fee may sue as an indigent; fee recovered if he wins.
stations.hook: No money ≠ no justice

stations.name: Interpleader
stations.one: A holder with no interest asks rival claimants to fight it out among themselves.
stations.hook: I hold it; you two decide whose it is

stations.name: Appeals
stations.one: First appeal on facts and law (S.96); second appeal only on a substantial question of law (S.100).
stations.boss: Santosh Hazari v Purushottam Tiwari (2001) — first appeal must deal with every issue
stations.hook: First: facts + law · Second: substantial law only

stations.name: Reference & review
stations.one: Lower court refers a legal doubt to the High Court; review for an error apparent, new evidence or sufficient reason.
stations.hook: Review = same judge, second look

stations.name: Revision
stations.one: High Court corrects jurisdictional errors of subordinate courts where no appeal lies.
stations.boss: Major S.S. Khanna v Brig. F.J. Dillon (1964) — ‘case decided’ explained
stations.hook: No appeal + jurisdiction error → revision

stations.name: Object of limitation
stations.one: Law helps the vigilant: limitation bars the remedy, not the right (except S.27).
stations.boss: Rajender Singh v Santa Singh (1973) — repose for settled claims
stations.hook: C-V-E-P: Certainty · Vigilance · Evidence · Peace

stations.name: S.3 — the bar
stations.one: A time-barred suit, appeal or application is dismissed even if no one raises limitation.
stations.boss: Bombay Dyeing v State of Bombay (1958) — limitation bars the remedy only
stations.hook: Court checks the clock itself

stations.name: Condonation of delay
stations.one: Late appeals and applications (not suits) admitted for sufficient cause — read liberally.
stations.boss: Collector, Anantnag v Mst. Katiji (1987) — substance over technicality
stations.hook: Applications yes · suits no

stations.name: Legal disability
stations.one: Minor, insane or idiot at the start: time runs from when disability ends (max 3 years extra); prison isn’t a disability.
stations.hook: M-I-I — not jail

stations.name: Computation
stations.one: Exclude the first day, time for copies, time in a wrong court in good faith, stays and notices.
stations.hook: Exclude · don’t extend

stations.name: Acknowledgment
stations.one: A written, signed acknowledgment before expiry gives a fresh period from its date.
stations.boss: Shapoor Freedom Mazda v Durga Prosad Chamaria (1961) — what counts as acknowledgment
stations.hook: Written · Signed · Before expiry

stations.name: Part-payment
stations.one: Payment by the debtor before expiry, shown in his writing, restarts the clock.
stations.hook: Pay a part, restart the clock

stations.name: Adverse possession
stations.one: 12 years’ hostile, open, continuous possession extinguishes the owner’s title.
stations.boss: Ravinder Kaur Grewal v Manjit Kaur (2019) — the possessor can also sue
stations.hook: Nec vi, nec clam, nec precario

xfer: a plaint in the wrong court is returned, not rejected
a late set-aside petition needs condonation (asked 2022)
appeals lie only from decrees and appealable orders
a minor is a party only through a next friend / guardian
two shields for property before judgment: attachment or injunction

routes.title: Can this suit be filed in this court?
steps: Is the dispute about a civil right (property, office, money, status)?
no
Not a civil suit — no jurisdiction (S.9).
Does a law expressly or impliedly bar civil courts (tribunal, special Act)?
yes
Barred — unless the authority acted illegally / ultra vires (Dhulabhai).
Is the claim within this court’s pecuniary limit?
no
Return the plaint to the proper court (O.VII r.10; S.6, 15).
Is the land, the wrong, the defendant or the cause of action within its territory?
no
Return the plaint (S.16–20, O.VII r.10).

routes.title: Is the second suit barred?
steps: Is the earlier suit still pending between the same parties on the same matter?
yes
Stay the later suit — res sub judice (S.10).
Was the same matter directly and substantially in issue before?
no
Not barred — unless it might and ought to have been raised (Expl. IV, constructive RJ).
Same parties (or those claiming under them), same title?
no
Not barred.
Was the earlier court competent, and did it hear and finally decide it?
no
Not barred.

routes.title: Ex parte decree passed — what now?
steps: Was the summons duly served?
no
Set aside under O.IX r.13 (not duly served).
Was there sufficient cause for not appearing?
yes
Set aside under O.IX r.13 — apply within 30 days (Art. 123).
Is the 30-day period over?
yes
Ask condonation with sufficient cause (S.5) — or appeal under S.96(2).
routes.end: Appeal (S.96(2)) or review — and defend on merits ✓

routes.title: Is the claim time-barred?
steps: Is it within the period in the Schedule (after excluding S.12–15 time)?
yes
In time ✓
Was the plaintiff a minor / insane / idiot when time began?
yes
Time runs after the disability ends (S.6–8).
Was there a written, signed acknowledgment or a part-payment before expiry?
yes
Fresh period from that date (S.18 / S.19).
Is it an appeal or application (not a suit) with sufficient cause for delay?
yes
Delay may be condoned (S.5).
routes.end: Dismissed under S.3 — and if possession: title extinguished after 12 years (S.27) ✗

routes.title: Party missing from the suit?
steps: Is he a necessary party — no effective decree without him?
no
Proper party only — suit proceeds; court may add him (O.I r.10).
Can he still be added (O.I r.10(2)), within limitation (S.21 Limitation Act)?
yes
Add him; suit continues against him from the date of joining.
routes.end: Suit fails for non-joinder of a necessary party (O.I r.9 proviso) ✗

routes.title: Can the defendant be arrested or his property attached before judgment?
steps: Is it a suit for immovable property (S.16 (a)–(d))?
yes
No arrest before judgment (O.XXXVIII r.1).
Is he absconding or leaving the court’s limits to delay or defeat the decree?
yes
Arrest / security for appearance (O.XXXVIII r.1–2).
Is he disposing of or removing his property to obstruct the decree?
yes
Attachment before judgment (O.XXXVIII r.5).
routes.end: No before-judgment order — use temporary injunction if property is at risk (O.XXXIX) ✓
